proof_summary: Assume divisibility holds eventually, and use Bertrand’s postulate to choose a sufficiently large prime \(p\); the minimal triangular-number block reaching \(2p\) contains the composite \(2p\), so its product is divisible by \(p\). A later block is arranged to lie strictly between \(2p\) and \(3p\), hence contains no multiple of \(p\), while eventual divisibility propagates the earlier product into the later one, giving a contradiction.
